argument: When individuals or replicators differ in heritable traits that affect survival or reproduction, trait frequencies change across generations. Selection can create adaptation without foresight by cumulatively retaining variants that reproduce better in the current environment.
boundary: Selection requires heritable variation and differential reproductive success.
Drift, mutation, migration, developmental constraints, and changing environments also shape evolution.
A trait can be a by-product, historical legacy, or neutral rather than an adaptation.
claim: When individuals or replicators differ in heritable traits that affect survival or reproduction, trait frequencies change across generations. Selection can create adaptation without foresight by cumulatively retaining variants that reproduce better in the current environment.
interpretation: Adaptationist stories are easy to invent after the fact. Principia should require fitness comparisons, heritability, and plausible historical alternatives.

title: Heritable Variation with Differential Reproduction Produces Adaptive Change
